method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE (an invalid scale amount answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Telecommunications (Consumer Protection and Service Standards) Act 1999, Compilation No. 45, compilation date 31 October 2025 (includes amendments up to Act No. 50, 2025), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A00441.txt. No instrument brought in: the customer service guarantee standard and scale (ss 115, 117), the USO determinations and standards, and the s 147 emergency call services determination are not deposited and are asked as facts where needed. Added 2026-10-23: the Telecommunications (Customer Service Guarantee) Standard 2023, Compilation No. 1 (F2026C00929), deposited at subjects/au/telecommunications-customer-service-guarantee-standard-2023, read by tcpss-csg-standard.l4.

scope: From the phone customer's seat: the universal service obligation to supply a standard telephone service on request and its exclusions (ss 6(1)(a)-(b), 9(1)(a), (2), (2AAA), (2C), (2E), (4), (6)), who supplies it (ss 12A as a fact, 12C, 12D(1)), the equipment (s 9E(1)); untimed local calls (ss 104-106, 108-110, zones as facts); the customer service guarantee: liability (ss 114, 115(2), 116(1), 120(2), (7)), the amount (ss 116(2)-(3), 117(3)), the time to sue (s 116(6)), the provider's times (s 117A), waiver (ss 120, 120A); the Ombudsman scheme (ss 127, 128(1), (4)-(7), 129-131). Out: payphones, the regulations under ss 6(1)(c) and 9E, s 107, s 112, the USO performance standards, wholesale standards and benchmarks, ss 118-119, Part 8 (emergency call services), Parts 2 (funding), 4, 9 and 9B. Broadband is Part 19 of the Telecommunications Act 1997, not this Act. Added 2026-10-23 (tcpss-csg-standard.l4): the CSG Standard 2023 ss 6, 10-15, 17, 19-27, 31 (as a fact), 32-34, 39, Schedules 1 and 2, with the provider's duties as regulative rules.
seat: the phone customer (a residential customer, small business or charity, and end-user of a carriage service)
